answer: The thread detector writes to velvet, and ripple makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 178 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 78 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
